objective: Initialize repository-level AppSDK Guidance for the agent-plugins monorepo. Guidance governs the four first-party plugin projects agent-tui, agent-memory, Teams, and dsh-concurrency-limit as one accumulating project context while preserving each plugin's local owner, contracts, maps, records, and lifecycle truth.

boundary.payload_control_separation: Plugin business payloads remain separate from routing, provider selection, retry, lifecycle, debug, snapshot, environment, control, and governance metadata. These control concerns use typed side channels and governance records only; no plugin may reconstruct control state from business payloads.

acceptance_criteria: The root AppSDK project is initialized from the current repository root with AppSDK 0.1.6 resources and no binary byte hash admission requirement.
Root Guidance is advisory and records recommendations without blocking ordinary small changes or inventing lifecycle evidence.

The feature workflow requires requirements -> map_check -> implementation -> candidate -> validation -> review -> integration -> cleanup; architecture, map_update, effectiveness, and promotion are explicit optional bypass nodes selected by risk and scope.

The debug workflow is orient -> explore -> resolve -> candidate -> validation -> review -> integration -> cleanup; orient reads AGENTS, maps, notes, records, and history, and explore always appends the current worker run notes.

Every debug task binds its issue to the actual function map and verification gates; a missing function map is recorded and repaired after the issue, while changed regression gates or map bindings are updated by their owner.

The root module registry represents agent-tui, Teams, and dsh-concurrency-limit as active project paths and represents agent-memory as pending until its canonical source is present on the root baseline; no missing path is presented as active.
Each task uses one clean owner worktree and, after delivery, reviews project AGENTS.md, local Skills, and MEMORY.md before removing only its own clean worktree.
non_goals: Do not modify deepseek-harness or the OpenCode reference source.
Do not merge, rewrite, delete, or reset child-project lifecycle records, maps, Active, Protected, claims, mailboxes, journals, or historical evidence as part of root Guidance bootstrap.
Do not replace child-project AppSDK contracts with a second lifecycle truth or copy a child project's maps into another project.
Do not make agent-memory active until its canonical source and governance contract are present on the root baseline.
Do not require every task to execute every advisory workflow node or create evidence for skipped low-risk detail.
assumptions: The repository root is the AppSDK project root and origin/main is the clean baseline for this bootstrap.

agent-tui and Teams retain their independent AppSDK 0.1.6 project contracts; dsh-concurrency-limit is a first-party plugin awaiting root and local governance binding; agent-memory remains represented as a pending fourth project until its source is merged.
The root maps describe cross-project ownership and workflow relationships; each child project's maps remain the canonical owner map for its own implementation and lifecycle.
The installed AppSDK 0.1.6 binary is used by version/contract compatibility, not by a hard-coded executable byte digest.

questions.question: Is this a repository governance bootstrap covering all first-party plugin projects?
questions.answer: Yes. The remote repository is the agent-plugins project; agent-tui is one module, and agent-memory, Teams, and dsh-concurrency-limit are the other first-party projects.

questions.question: Which relative directory is the AppSDK project root?
questions.answer: The current repository root, relative path .

questions.question: Which existing directories remain read-only and outside root Guidance ownership?
questions.answer: deepseek-harness, the ignored OpenCode reference, repository workflows, child-project lifecycle truth, and other workers' worktrees/claims/records remain unchanged and read-only for this bootstrap.

questions.question: Which directories may root Guidance create or modify?
questions.answer: Only root AppSDK governance, root documents/Skills, root maps, and explicitly declared first-party project bindings; child-project source and lifecycle truth remain with their own owners.

questions.question: How strongly should Guidance enforce the workflow?
questions.answer: advisory: guide plan/update/next records recommendations and status, while small tasks may skip unnecessary detail and evidence.

questions.question: What context is mandatory for each debug task?
questions.answer: orient reads AGENTS, resource/function/mainline/verification maps, notes, records, and history; explore appends run notes; resolve binds the fix and any regression/map update to the unique owner and gate.

questions.question: What happens when a task ends?
questions.answer: The owner reviews AGENTS.md, local Skills, and MEMORY.md, retains historical evidence, and removes only its own merged, clean worktree after the required receipt.
